boundary: S8 foundational comparison control. Retrieves scholarly foundations for Story Point and relative-effort validity, multidimensional developer productivity, human code review, subjective mental-workload measurement, and software-delivery flow/queue interpretation. Method and instrument records are retained in the method/reference stratum and are not GenAI primary studies. Developmental only; not a frozen search, screening decision, eligibility decision, PRISMA input, or empirical support for VDCM.

queries.query: ((("story point" OR "relative estimate") AND (effort OR agile)) OR "developer productivity" OR "software developers perceptions of productivity" OR "modern code review" OR "NASA-TLX" OR ("mental workload" AND performance) OR ("Little's law" AND software))

+((("story point" | "relative estimate") + (effort | agile)) | "developer productivity" | "software developers perceptions of productivity" | "modern code review" | "NASA TLX" | ("mental workload" + performance) | ("Little's law" + software))

sentinels.title: Story points changes in agile iterative development
sentinels.rationale: Empirically demonstrates that Story Point estimates can change with evolving work-item information and directly bounds reliability assumptions.

sentinels.title: Software developers' perceptions of productivity
sentinels.rationale: Foundational empirical evidence that developer productivity includes task completion, interruptions, and context switching rather than code output alone.

sentinels.title: Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review
sentinels.rationale: Foundational socio-technical evidence that code review includes understanding, knowledge transfer, and team awareness as well as defect finding.

sentinels.title: NASA-Task Load Index (NASA-TLX); 20 Years Later
sentinels.rationale: Defines the retrospective multidimensional subjective-workload instrument used only as a construct comparator, not as an ex-ante capacity estimator.

sentinels.title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = lambda W
sentinels.rationale: Foundational queueing identity used only to interpret flow conservation under its assumptions, not to claim empirical software-delivery validity.

sentinels.title: Relative estimates of software development effort: Are they more accurate or less time-consuming to produce than absolute estimates, and to what extent are they person-independent?
sentinels.rationale: Directly tests claimed benefits and person-independence of relative estimates, preventing an assumed-failure or assumed-superiority narrative.

sentinels.title: Workload and Performance: Associations, Insensitivities, and Dissociations
sentinels.rationale: Constrains any inference that measured workload and task performance are interchangeable constructs.

sentinels.title: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration-task load index: NASA-TLX: evaluation of its use in surgery
sentinels.rationale: A legitimate workload study outside software engineering; retrieval is a precision warning rather than evidence for the framework.
